extracted.intended_audience: telecom providers, industry stakeholders, legal counsel, and public commenters on FCC robocall rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of Federal Register entries (rules, proposed rules, notices) describing standards, procedural requirements, and enforcement measures the FCC is proposing or adopting to combat illegal robocalls, maintain the Robocall Mitigation Database, and protect consumers. Useful for preparing comments, ensuring compliance, or analyzing regulatory policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robocall Mitigation Database accuracy, completeness, and currentness
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires Robocall Mitigation Database (RMD or Database) filers to take additional steps to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and currentness of submitted information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Database is a key tool for ensuring compliance with STIR/SHAKEN and robocall mitigation rules and for enforcement; proposals include procedural steps, technical validation, and accountability measures to increase the Database's effectiveness as a compliance and consumer protection tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture penalties for false or inaccurate RMD submissions and failures to update
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a base forfeiture of $10,000 for each violation for filers that submit false or inaccurate information to the Database, and a base forfeiture of $1,000 for failure to update information that has changed in the Database within 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an enforcement mechanism to promote truthful, timely filings; tied to proposed or adopted rulemaking (includes direction to assess and apply base forfeitures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-factor (or more) authentication for Database access
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct the Wireline Competition Bureau and Office of the Managing Director to develop a two-factor (or more) authentication solution for accessing the Robocall Mitigation Database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to increase account security and reduce misuse of access to numbering and certification data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated reporting mechanism and best practices for deficient RMD filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a dedicated reporting mechanism for deficient filings in the Database and issue additional guidance and 'best practices' for filers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an administrative path for identifying and remediating deficient submissions and provides expectations for improved filing diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file robocall mitigation plans and certifications in the RMD
rubrics_metrics.description: All providers are required to file certifications and robocall mitigation plans in the Robocall Mitigation Database; certifications lacking required information or mitigation plans are deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must cure deficiencies or explain why certification should not be removed; removal from the RMD can require intermediate providers and voice service providers to cease accepting calls directly from that company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of consent to robocalls and robotexts — manner and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation of consent can be made in any reasonable manner, and callers must honor do-not-call and consent revocation requests within a reasonable time not to exceed ten business days of receipt; text senders are limited to a one-time confirmation text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amends rules to make it simpler for consumers to revoke consent and requires prompt compliance by callers and texters; codifies practical limits on confirmation messaging for texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCPA application to wireless providers' calls to their own subscribers
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on whether the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) applies to robocalls and robotexts from wireless providers to their own subscribers and whether wireless subscribers can exercise their right to revoke such consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores the scope of TCPA obligations for providers calling their own customers (telecom carriers) and whether these calls require consent or are exempt; seeks input on revocation rights in this context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated opt-out mechanisms on artificial/prerecorded voice calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on requiring automated opt-out mechanisms on every call that uses an artificial or prerecorded voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would provide consumers an on-call means to opt out when receiving automated/prerecorded calls; part of proposals to strengthen consumer protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering policies to limit misuse of assigned numbering resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose changes to numbering policies regarding how assigned numbering resources are utilized, reported, and resold by service providers to reduce access to telephone numbers by potential perpetrators of illegal robocalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions are proposed pursuant to the Commission's numbering administration authority and in furtherance of TRACED Act obligations; aims to safeguard numbering resources, protect consumers, and address resellers that facilitate illegal robocalling schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmit verified caller name / use Rich Call Data for A-level attestations
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose requiring terminating providers to transmit verified caller name or other caller identity information for presentation on a consumer's handset whenever they transmit an indication that a call has received an A-level attestation, and to use Rich Call Data (RCD) to transmit verified caller name on IP networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks to enhance STIR/SHAKEN effectiveness by providing consumers better caller identity information; asks whether to permit or require RCD implementations or other solutions, and whether RCD should be required for all calls on IP networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark international calls and prohibit spoofing of U.S. numbers from abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose measures to ensure consumers know which calls originate from outside the United States and to prohibit spoofing of United States telephone numbers for calls that originate from outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at reducing fraud and consumer confusion from foreign-origin spoofed calls; may involve labeling, network-based controls, or prohibitions on certain spoofing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and possible revision of STIR/SHAKEN implementation and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on whether extensions for implementation of the STIR/SHAKEN caller ID authentication framework should be revised or extended and to inform the Commission's triennial assessment of STIR/SHAKEN's efficacy as a tool to combat illegal robocalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes evaluating what standard should be used to assess STIR/SHAKEN's impact and whether to maintain, revise, or replace that standard; recognizes STIR/SHAKEN as one facet of a larger enforcement campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocking based on reasonable Do-Not-Originate (DNO) lists and SIP 603+ behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Require all domestic voice service providers to block calls based on a reasonable do-not-originate (DNO) list and to return Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) code 603+ when calls are blocked based on reasonable analytics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands blocking obligations to all U.S.-based providers and standardizes signaling behavior (SIP 603+) to indicate blocked calls to downstream systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define AI-generated calls and require disclosure and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to define AI-generated calls, adopt rules requiring callers to disclose to consumers when they receive an AI-generated call, and adopt protections to ensure callers apprise consumers of AI use when consumers affirmatively consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also seeks protections to allow beneficial AI uses (e.g., accessibility for people with disabilities), and requests comment on technologies that can alert consumers to unwanted or illegal AI-generated calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical validation solutions and procedural diligence for RMD filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose procedural measures requiring RMD filers to take additional steps, including potential technical solutions for validating data, to improve overall quality and accountability of submissions in the Robocall Mitigation Database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include automated data validation, cross-checks with other registries, and procedural requirements intended to detect and prevent inaccurate or stale filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act system of records rescindment for RMD
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to rescind the FCC/WCB-5, Robocall Mitigation Database, system of records under the Privacy Act of 1974; the system previously collected information from individual representatives certifying STIR/SHAKEN implementation and robocall mitigation programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative change affecting how the FCC treats and maintains personally identifiable information associated with RMD certifications and representative contact data; rescindment becomes effective 30 days after publication unless otherwise noted.
